entries.title: Peeling Painted Wall
entries.author: Dimitrios Savva
entries.note: Real photographed/scanned surface with muted coral-red paint, fine cracks and irregular pale exposed patches. Use 2k detail only on near-camera painted wall patches or a small worn panel, not as a replacement for every regional facade. Diffuse is sRGB; OpenGL normal and roughness are linear data. These JPGs are opaque full surface maps, not alpha decals; localized blending needs a separate mask or bounded geometry. The source paint color is visible and should not be mistaken for a neutral wear-only layer. All source bytes and API MD5 checksums verified.

entries.title: Worn Plaster Wall
entries.author: Dimitrios Savva
entries.note: Real photographed/scanned gray-beige plaster with irregular missing finish, darker substrate, streaking and a conspicuous vertical seam. Suitable for a small close-up lower-wall wear patch; crop or position the seam deliberately instead of repeating it across unrelated masonry. It does not depict exposed brick courses. 2k is reserved for local damage detail. Diffuse is sRGB; OpenGL normal and roughness are linear data. Opaque JPG surface maps require separate masking for decal-like use. All source bytes and API MD5 checksums verified.

entries.title: Wood Peeling Paint Weathered
entries.author: Dimitrios Savva (photography); Rob Tuytel (processing)
entries.note: Real photographed/scanned timber with dark blue-black paint worn away along warm brown grain. Useful on a close-up boatyard workbench, shutter, worn door or painted wooden panel. Align the visible horizontal grain with the modeled timber; do not scatter it as an orientation-free wall decal. 2k provides local chipped-paint detail without a 4k pack. Diffuse is sRGB; OpenGL normal and roughness are linear data. Opaque JPG surface maps, with source color retained; all source bytes and API MD5 checksums verified.

entries.title: Planter Pot Clay
entries.author: Amal Kumar
entries.note: Complete original glTF 2.0 package: one mesh, one double-sided material, local binary geometry and all three local 2k texture dependencies. A realistically weathered, empty terracotta planter with a tapered body, rolled rim, interior and worn pale deposits; no plant is included. Appropriate for one close-up terrace or workshop prop at roughly 27cm wide and 22cm tall. Load files.gltf and preserve its sibling paths; no runtime network or decoder dependency. ARM uses red=ambient occlusion, green=roughness, blue=metalness; the original glTF binds metallic/roughness but does not separately bind ambient occlusion. Poly Haven verifies creator and CC0 rights but does not specify the capture technique in its asset metadata: this is not represented as verified photogrammetry. Source previews and the supplied texture/mesh data were inspected; all five files retain their original API-verified bytes and MD5 hashes.

entries.title: Leaf001 - photographic broadleaf
entries.author: ambientCG (individual photographer not identified in the asset record)
entries.note: Created using Leaf001 from ambientCG.com, licensed under the Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal License. · Actual photographic foliage, not botanical illustration: two side-by-side views of a serrated green broadleaf with clear branching veins, fine surface texture and stem. ambientCG identifies its method as height field photogrammetry. Species and leaf-side identity are not specified. Select one half of the atlas per leaf, using the same UV region for diffuse, normal and roughness; do not map the entire two-leaf sheet onto one leaf. Diffuse RGB is sRGB, while alpha/normal/roughness are linear data. Use the supplied silhouette with alpha testing and curved leaf geometry rather than broad flat rectangular cards. This is not a palm, banana leaf or rice blade. The source JPEG opacity may contain near-zero compression specks; an alpha-test cutoff removes them without changing the preserved originals.

entries.title: Grass Medium 02 - photographic blade atlas
entries.author: Rico Cilliers
entries.note: Actual photographic grass-blade texture from Poly Haven's Grass Medium 02 model: isolated green and straw-brown blades with lengthwise surface detail, natural bends, curled tips and worn edges. Texture resources only; no grass model was downloaded. Select a single blade's UV region and use the same region on all maps, then fit curved or folded geometry to its silhouette. The whole atlas is not one tuft or one palm frond. Diffuse RGB is sRGB; alpha, OpenGL normal and roughness are linear data. This supplies the requested narrow grass-leaf option; it is not a verified palm leaflet or species-specific rice texture.

entries.title: Kloppenheim 03 PureSky
entries.author: Greg Zaal (original photography); Jarod Guest (sky edits)
entries.note: Photographic midday pure sky with blue openings, broken high white clouds and neutral daylight, not a sunset or landmark panorama. The complete decoded panorama was tone-mapped for inspection: no houses, buildings, terrain or recognizable landmarks were visible. Poly Haven's credited sky edits remove the original ground; the lower hemisphere is a softened continuation of sky colors, not a photographic sea or ground surface. Use as a visible sky/background option while keeping the existing overcast_soil lighting baseline and actual 3D terrain/buildings. Favor the upper hemisphere above the modeled horizon; align sky rotation with scene lighting as appropriate. The original Radiance RGBE HDR is unmodified, with API byte count and MD5 verified; tone mapping was inspection-only and no generated sky pixels or preview files are distributed.

entries.title: Kloofendal 43d Clear (Pure Sky)
entries.author: Greg Zaal
entries.note: Photographic clear blue sky with a high sun and light horizon haze, photographed in South Africa, not the Douro. The full panorama was decoded and inspected; its lower hemisphere is a softened sky continuation, not a photographed river or landscape. The original HDR is unchanged. Terrain, buildings and water remain modeled; sun direction and reflections follow the selected sky. Tone mapping was used only for local inspection.

entries.title: Boulder 01
entries.author: Rico Cilliers
entries.note: Actual textured 3D boulder with jagged gray-and-rust facets, natural crevices and an irregular silhouette, not a background photograph or generated blob. Selected instead of rock_boulder_dry, which is a surface texture rather than a model; the explicitly coastal formation candidate exceeded the size budget. Suitable as a generic weathered shoreline rock in the fictional scene, not a claimed Tunisian geological specimen. Complete original glTF 2.0 package with its binary mesh and all three local 1k PBR maps; no external runtime dependencies or compression decoder. Load files.gltf with sibling paths intact and retain its UV-matched textures rather than substituting the existing tiling rock maps. ARM packs red=ambient occlusion, green=roughness, blue=metalness; the original material binds metallic/roughness but not separate ambient occlusion. Metrics are measured from this packaged glTF, not the catalog's different polygon count. Its local minimum Y is about -0.073643m, so use transformed bounds when placing it on the shore. Limit near-camera instances or add integration-side LOD: each copy renders 66,122 triangles. All five source files are unmodified and API-MD5 verified; no preview render is retained.

entries.title: Vitis vinifera — Köhler's Medizinal-Pflanzen, plate 51 (1887)
entries.author: Brandt, Wilhelm; Gürke, M.; Köhler, F. E.; Pabst, G.; Schellenberg, G.; Vogtherr, Max. (Biodiversity Heritage Library catalog attribution)
entries.license: Public domain (PD-scan; PD-old-70-1923)
entries.note: Grapevine with a green grape cluster, lobed leaves, curling tendrils and botanical detail studies on warm aged paper. entries.text: In Marrakech, a riad turns the home inward, around a courtyard open to the sky. Shade, water, and plants temper the heat and create privacy within the dense streets of the medina.
